authoredSolutions.1: Let \(A\) be the rightward acceleration of the big block \(M\) and let \(a\) be the upward acceleration of \(m_{2}\). Since \(m_{2}\) rises, the string on its side shortens, so \(m_{1}\) slides backward relative to \(M\) with the same magnitude \(a\); the ground acceleration of \(m_{1}\) is therefore \(A-a\), while \(m_{2}\) is pressed by the vertical face of \(M\) and shares the horizontal acceleration \(A\). For \(m_{2}\) vertically, \[T-m_{2}g=m_{2}a\;\Rightarrow\;T=20(10+2)=240\text{ N}.\] For \(m_{1}\) horizontally (the top surface is frictionless), \[T=m_{1}(A-a)\;\Rightarrow\;240=10(A-2)\;\Rightarrow\;A=26\text{ ms}^{-2}.\] Applying Newton's second law to the whole system horizontally, \[F=MA+m_{1}(A-a)+m_{2}A=100(26)+10(24)+20(26)=2600+240+520=3360\text{ N}.\] So the correct choice is A. Note that \(3380\text{ N}=130A\) is exactly what one gets by wrongly assuming \(m_{1}\) also moves with \(A\).
authoredSolutions.2: For an electromagnetic wave \(\lambda=c/f\). \[\lambda_{1}=\frac{3\times10^{8}}{6\times10^{6}}=50\text{ m},\qquad \lambda_{2}=\frac{3\times10^{8}}{10\times10^{6}}=30\text{ m}.\] The wavelength bandwidth is \(\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}=50-30=20\text{ m}\), so the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.3: Activity decays as \(A=A_{0}e^{-\lambda t}\), so \[\lambda=\frac{1}{t}\ln\frac{A_{0}}{A}=\frac{1}{10}\ln\frac{4250}{2250}=\frac{1}{10}\ln(1.888).\] Using \(\ln x=2.303\log_{10}x\) and the given \(\log_{10}1.88=0.274\), \[\lambda=\frac{2.303\times0.274}{10}=0.063\ \min^{-1}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.4: Energy incident per second on area \(A\) is \(IA\), and each photon carries \(hc/\lambda\). Hence \[n=\frac{IA\lambda}{hc}=\frac{(100)(1\times10^{-4})(900\times10^{-9})}{(6.63\times10^{-34})(3\times10^{8})}=\frac{9\times10^{-9}}{1.99\times10^{-25}}\approx4.5\times10^{16}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.5: Fringe width is \(\beta=\lambda D/d\), and in a medium of refractive index \(\mu\) the wavelength becomes \(\lambda/\mu\). Therefore \[\beta_{\text{water}}=\frac{\beta_{\text{air}}}{\mu}=\frac{12}{4/3}=9\text{ mm}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.6: For a plane electromagnetic wave \(E_{0}=cB_{0}\), so \[E_{0}=(3\times10^{8})(2\times10^{-8})=6\text{ Vm}^{-1}.\] The phase is \((kx+\omega t)\), so the wave travels along \(-\widehat{x}\). Since \(\widehat{E}\times\widehat{B}\) points along the propagation direction and \(\widehat{B}=\widehat{j}\), we need \(\widehat{E}\times\widehat{j}=-\widehat{i}\), which is satisfied by \(\widehat{E}=\widehat{k}\). Hence the field is \(6\text{ Vm}^{-1}\) along the \(z\)-axis and the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.7: For the \(LR\) circuit, \(Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+X_{L}^{2}}=\sqrt{2}R\) since \(X_{L}=R\), so \[P_{1}=\cos\phi=\frac{R}{Z}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\] Adding \(C\) with \(X_{C}=X_{L}\) brings the circuit to resonance, so \(Z=R\) and \(P_{2}=1\). Hence \(\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.8: The magnetic force \(\overrightarrow{F}=q(\overrightarrow{v}\times\overrightarrow{B})\) is always perpendicular to \(\overrightarrow{B}\), and so is the acceleration. Therefore \[\overrightarrow{a}\cdot\overrightarrow{B}=0\;\Rightarrow\;(\alpha\widehat{i}-4\widehat{j})\cdot(2\widehat{i}+3\widehat{j})=0,\] which gives \(2\alpha-12=0\), i.e. \(\alpha=6\). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.9: At the centre of a circular coil, \(B=\frac{\mu_{0}Ni}{2R}\). Both coils have the same radius \(20\text{ cm}\) and carry the same current, so \[\frac{B_{X}}{B_{Y}}=\frac{N_{X}}{N_{Y}}=\frac{200}{400}=\frac{1}{2}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.10: The four \(4\ \Omega\) resistors form a Wheatstone bridge with the \(2\ \Omega\) resistor as the bridge arm. Since \(\frac{4}{4}=\frac{4}{4}\), the bridge is balanced and no current flows through the \(2\ \Omega\) resistor, so it can be removed. The two arms are then \(4+4=8\ \Omega\) each, in parallel: \[R_{\text{net}}=\frac{8\times8}{8+8}=4\ \Omega,\qquad I=\frac{40}{4}=10\text{ A}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.11: Capacitors in parallel all share the same \(20\text{ V}\), and the total charge is \[Q=(C_{1}+C_{2}+C_{3}+C_{4})V=(1+2+4+3)\ \mu F\times20\text{ V}=200\ \mu C.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.12: In SHM the speed depends on displacement as \(v=\omega\sqrt{A^{2}-x^{2}}\). Squaring and rearranging, \[\frac{v^{2}}{(\omega A)^{2}}+\frac{x^{2}}{A^{2}}=1,\] which is the equation of an ellipse in the \(v\)-\(x\) plane (a circle only if \(\omega=1\)). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.13: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, so \(\Delta U=nC_{V}\Delta T\) whatever the process. For a monatomic gas \(C_{V}=\frac{3R}{2}\), hence \[\Delta U=7\times\frac{3}{2}\times8.3\times40=3486\text{ J}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.14: Constant entropy means the compression is adiabatic, so \(PV^{\gamma}=\) constant with \(\gamma=5/3\) for a monatomic gas. With \(V_{2}=V/8\), \[P_{2}=P\left(\frac{V}{V/8}\right)^{5/3}=P\cdot8^{5/3}=P\cdot2^{5}=32P.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.15: Volume is conserved, so \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^{3}=729\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}\), giving \(r=R/9\). The gain in surface energy is \[\Delta U=T\left(729\cdot4\pi r^{2}-4\pi R^{2}\right)=4\pi R^{2}T(9-1).\] With \(T=75\text{ dyne/cm}=0.075\text{ Nm}^{-1}\) and \(R=10^{-2}\text{ m}\), \[\Delta U=4(3.14)(10^{-4})(0.075)(8)=7.5\times10^{-4}\text{ J}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.16: For \(h\ll R\), \(g'=g\left(1-\frac{2h}{R}\right)\), so the fractional decrease in weight is \[\frac{\Delta g}{g}=\frac{2h}{R}=\frac{2\times32}{6400}=0.01.\] That is a decrease of \(1\%\), so the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.17: The two equal masses move apart with equal speeds, so the centre of mass stays at rest and both are momentarily at rest when the elongation is maximum. Energy conservation then gives \[2\times\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}.\] With \(m=0.25\text{ kg}\) and \(k=2\text{ Nm}^{-1}\), \(0.25v^{2}=x^{2}\), so \(x=\frac{v}{2}\). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.18: Climbing down with \(a=4\text{ ms}^{-2}\): \(mg-T=ma\), so \[T=50(10-4)=300\text{ N}<350\text{ N},\] and the rope holds. Climbing up with \(a=5\text{ ms}^{-2}\): \(T-mg=ma\), so \[T=50(10+5)=750\text{ N}>350\text{ N}.\] The rope therefore breaks while the monkey climbs upward, and the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.19: Time to reach maximum height is \(t=\frac{u\sin\theta}{g}\). Equal times require \[u_{1}\sin30^{\circ}=u_{2}\sin45^{\circ}\;\Rightarrow\;\frac{u_{1}}{u_{2}}=\frac{\sin45^{\circ}}{\sin30^{\circ}}=\frac{1/\sqrt{2}}{1/2}=\sqrt{2}.\] The ratio is \(\sqrt{2}:1\), so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.20: Least count \(=\frac{\text{pitch}}{\text{divisions}}=\frac{0.5}{50}=0.01\text{ mm}\). The diameter is \[D=1.5+7(0.01)=1.57\text{ mm}=0.157\text{ cm}.\] The curved surface area of the wire is \[\pi D\ell=3.14\times0.157\times6.8=3.35\ \text{cm}^{2}\approx3.4\ \text{cm}^{2}\] to two significant figures. The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.21: Given \(u_{x}=1\text{ ms}^{-1}\) and \(y=5x(1-x)\), differentiate with respect to time: \[\frac{dy}{dt}=5\frac{dx}{dt}-10x\frac{dx}{dt}.\] At launch \(x=0\) and \(\frac{dx}{dt}=1\), so \(u_{y}=5\text{ ms}^{-1}\). The initial \(y\)-component of velocity is \(5\widehat{j}\), i.e. the value is 5.
authoredSolutions.22: The particle starts at the top of the disc and falls a height \(2R\) to the lowest point. The moment of inertia of the system about the axis is \[I=\frac{mR^{2}}{2}+mR^{2}=\frac{3}{2}mR^{2}.\] Energy conservation gives \[mg(2R)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{3}{2}mR^{2}\omega^{2}\;\Rightarrow\;\omega^{2}=\frac{8g}{3R}=\frac{80}{3R}.\] Comparing with \(\omega=4\sqrt{\frac{x}{3R}}\), i.e. \(\omega^{2}=\frac{16x}{3R}\), we get \(16x=80\), so \(x=5\).
authoredSolutions.23: Young's modulus is \(Y=\frac{FL}{A\,\Delta L}\) with \(A=\frac{\pi d^{2}}{4}\). Substituting \(F=10\text{ N}\), \(L=1\text{ m}\), \(d=\Delta L=0.4\times10^{-3}\text{ m}\), \[Y=\frac{4(10)(1)}{\pi(0.4\times10^{-3})^{2}(0.4\times10^{-3})}=1.99\times10^{11}\ \text{Nm}^{-2}.\] The fractional error is \[\frac{\Delta Y}{Y}=\frac{\Delta(\Delta L)}{\Delta L}+2\frac{\Delta d}{d}=\frac{0.02}{0.4}+2\left(\frac{0.01}{0.4}\right)=0.05+0.05=0.1.\] Hence \(\Delta Y=0.1\times1.99\times10^{11}=1.99\times10^{10}\approx2\times10^{10}\ \text{Nm}^{-2}\), so \(x=2\).
authoredSolutions.24: Approaching: \(f_{1}=f_{0}\frac{c}{c-v_{s}}=100\). Receding: \(f_{2}=f_{0}\frac{c}{c+v_{s}}=50\). Dividing, \[\frac{c+v_{s}}{c-v_{s}}=2\;\Rightarrow\;v_{s}=\frac{c}{3}.\] Substituting back, \[100=f_{0}\frac{c}{c-c/3}=\frac{3}{2}f_{0}\;\Rightarrow\;f_{0}=\frac{200}{3}\text{ Hz}.\] An observer moving with the car hears the source frequency \(f_{0}=\frac{200}{3}\text{ Hz}\), so \(x=200\).
authoredSolutions.25: The foil splits the capacitor into two capacitors in series. From the figure \(\epsilon_{r1}=3,\ t_{1}=0.5\text{ mm}\) and \(\epsilon_{r2}=4,\ t_{2}=1\text{ mm}\), with a \(100\text{ V}\) supply. Writing \(C=\frac{\epsilon_{r}\epsilon_{0}A}{t}\) in units of \(\epsilon_{0}A\) per mm, \[C_{1}=\frac{3}{0.5}=6,\qquad C_{2}=\frac{4}{1}=4.\] In series, \(C_{\text{eq}}=\frac{6\times4}{6+4}=2.4\), so the common charge is \(q=2.4\times100=240\). The potential drop across the second slab is \[V_{2}=\frac{q}{C_{2}}=\frac{240}{4}=60\text{ V},\] which is the potential of the foil measured from the earthed plate. Hence the answer is 60.
authoredSolutions.26: From the figure \(P=4\ \Omega\). At the first balance point, \[\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{l_{1}}{100-l_{1}}=\frac{40}{60}=\frac{2}{3}\;\Rightarrow\;Q=6\ \Omega.\] With \(X\) in series with \(P\) the new balance is at \(80\text{ cm}\), so \[\frac{P+X}{Q}=\frac{80}{20}=4\;\Rightarrow\;P+X=24\ \Omega.\] Therefore \(X=24-4=20\ \Omega\).
authoredSolutions.27: At very high frequency \(X_{C}=\frac{1}{\omega C}\to0\), so every capacitor behaves as a short circuit, while \(X_{L}=\omega L\to\infty\), so every inductor behaves as an open circuit. Branch by branch, the first section reduces to the \(1\ \Omega\) resistor alone (its inductive branch is open), the second section to \(4\ \Omega\parallel4\ \Omega=2\ \Omega\), and the third to the \(2\ \Omega\) resistor alone. Hence \[Z=1+2+2=5\ \Omega,\qquad I=\frac{220}{5}=44\text{ A}.\]
authoredSolutions.28: From the graph, when \(\frac{1}{u}=0\) the intercept is \(\frac{1}{v}=0.10\ \text{cm}^{-1}\); by the lens equation \(\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\), this intercept is \(\frac{1}{f}\), so \(f=10\text{ cm}\). For an equiconvex lens \(R_{1}=R\), \(R_{2}=-R\), so the lensmaker's formula gives \[\frac{1}{f}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right)=(1.5-1)\frac{2}{R}=\frac{1}{R}.\] Hence \(R=f=10\text{ cm}\).
authoredSolutions.29: First Lyman line \((2\to1)\): \(\frac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(1-\frac{1}{4}\right)=\frac{3R}{4}\), so \(\lambda=\frac{4}{3R}\). Third Paschen line \((6\to3)\): \(\frac{1}{\lambda_{3}}=R\left(\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{36}\right)=\frac{R}{12}\), so \(\lambda_{3}=\frac{12}{R}\). Second Balmer line \((4\to2)\): \(\frac{1}{\lambda_{2}}=R\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right)=\frac{3R}{16}\), so \(\lambda_{2}=\frac{16}{3R}\). The difference is \[\lambda_{3}-\lambda_{2}=\frac{12}{R}-\frac{16}{3R}=\frac{20}{3R}=a\lambda=a\cdot\frac{4}{3R},\] giving \(a=5\).
authoredSolutions.30: The load current is fixed by the zener voltage: \[I_{L}=\frac{V_{Z}}{R_{L}}=\frac{60}{10\times10^{3}}=6\text{ mA}.\] The zener current is largest when the input is largest, \(120\text{ V}\): \[I=\frac{120-60}{4\times10^{3}}=15\text{ mA}.\] Hence \(I_{Z}=I-I_{L}=15-6=9\text{ mA}\).
authoredSolutions.62: Right angle at \(A\), \(OA=AB\Rightarrow z_2=z_1(1+i)=-1+3i\) (Re \(<0\)). Then \(|2z_1-z_2|=|3+i|=\sqrt{10}\neq5\), so (D) is NOT true (A,B,C all hold).
authoredSolutions.63: Infinite solutions \(\Rightarrow\) eq3 \(=\) eq1\(-4\)eq2, so \(\lambda=4,\mu=-2\). Distance of \((4,-2,-\tfrac12)\) from \(8x+y+4z+2=0\): \(|32-2-2+2|/\sqrt{81}=30/9=10/3\).
authoredSolutions.64: For \(2\times2\) with \(t=\mathrm{tr}A,d=\det A=-1\): \(\det(A+I)=1+t+d=t\) and \(\det(\mathrm{adj}A+I)=t\). So \(t^2=4\Rightarrow t=\pm2\); \(2\) is available.
authoredSolutions.67: Numerator \(=\ln((1+x^2)^2-x^2)=\ln(1+x^2+x^4)\sim x^2\); denominator \(=\sec x-\cos x=\sin^2x/\cos x\sim x^2\). Limit \(k=1\).
authoredSolutions.69: Left branch has \(g'(x)=3x^2-2x+10>0\) (increasing), \(f(1)=3\). Right branch decreasing; need \(3\ge-2+\log_2(b^2-4)\Rightarrow b^2\le36\) with \(b^2>4\). Hence \(b\in[-6,-2)\cup(2,6]\).
authoredSolutions.71: IF \(=\sec^2x\); \(y\sec^2x=\sec x+C\Rightarrow y=\cos x+C\cos^2x\). \(y(\pi/3)=0\Rightarrow C=-2\), \(y=\cos x-2\cos^2x\). Max at \(\cos x=1/4\): \(y=\tfrac14-\tfrac18=\tfrac18\).
authoredSolutions.72: Locus: \(x^2+y^2+x-3y-2=0\). x-axis chord \(AB=3\) (roots \(-2,1\)); y-axis chord \(CD=\sqrt{17}\). Diagonals perpendicular: area \(=\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot\sqrt{17}=\tfrac{3\sqrt{17}}{2}\).
authoredSolutions.75: \(\vec a\times\vec b=(1-\alpha,\ \alpha^2-2,\ \alpha-2)\). Projection on \((-\hat i+2\hat j-2\hat k)\) (\(|c|=3\)): \((2\alpha^2-\alpha-1)/3=30\Rightarrow2\alpha^2-\alpha-91=0\Rightarrow\alpha=7\).

authoredSolutions.81: Disc \(=-4(pr-q^2)^2\le0\Rightarrow pr=q^2\), double root \(=q/p=t\in\{2,-4\}\). \((q^2+r^2)/p^2=t^2+t^4\). \(t=2\Rightarrow p,q,r\) same sign (excluded); \(t=-4\Rightarrow16+256=272\).
authoredSolutions.83: Set \(n\) ends at the \(n^2\)-th multiple of 3 and has \(2n-1\) terms. 11th set: multiples indexed \(101\ldots121\). Sum \(=3\sum_{m=101}^{121}m=3\cdot\tfrac{(101+121)\cdot21}{2}=3\cdot2331=6993\).
authoredSolutions.84: Expand: \(x^8-x^7-x^6+x^5+3x^4-4x^3-2x^2+4x-1\). Sign analysis gives simple roots at \(x=-1\) and \(x\approx0.4\), and a double (touch) root at \(x=1\). Distinct real roots \(=3\).
authoredSolutions.87: \(\int_3^x y\,dx=(y/x)^3\); differentiate with \(u=y/x\Rightarrow u\,u'=x/3\Rightarrow u^2=x^2/3-2\), so \(y^2=x^4/3-2x^2\). \(y=6\sqrt{10}\Rightarrow\alpha^4/3-2\alpha^2=360\Rightarrow\alpha^2=36,\ \alpha=6\).
authoredSolutions.88: \(A=(1,-2)\). Altitude from \(A\perp BC\Rightarrow p=a+2\); altitude from \(C\perp AB\Rightarrow y_C=2a+1=(15a-3)/(p+1)\Rightarrow a^2-4a+3=0\), \(a=1\) (in range). \(p=3\); orthocentre checks as \((2,1)\).
authoredSolutions.89: \(f'=4x-1/x=0\Rightarrow a=\tfrac12\), parabola \(y^2=2x\). Tangent \(ty=x+t^2/2\) through \((4,3)\Rightarrow t^2-6t+8=0\); \(t=2\) passes \((-2,0)\) (excluded), so \(t=4\), \(P=(8,4)\). Normal \(4x+y=36\Rightarrow x/9+y/36=1\), \(\alpha+\beta=45\).
authoredSolutions.91: Range is \(R=\frac{u^{2}\sin2\theta}{g}\), so for the same speed \[\frac{R_{45}}{R_{30}}=\frac{\sin90^{\circ}}{\sin60^{\circ}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}/2}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\] The ratio is \(2:\sqrt{3}\), so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.92: With \(10\) V.S.D. \(=9\) M.S.D. and \(1\) M.S.D. \(=1\text{ mm}\), the least count is \[\text{L.C.}=1-0.9=0.1\text{ mm}=0.01\text{ cm}.\] The vernier zero lies to the left of the main-scale zero with the \(4^{\text{th}}\) division coinciding, so the zero error is negative: \[e=-(10-4)\times0.1=-0.6\text{ mm}=-0.06\text{ cm}.\] The observed reading is \(30\times1\text{ mm}+6\times0.1\text{ mm}=3.06\text{ cm}\), and the corrected diameter is \[3.06-(-0.06)=3.12\text{ cm}.\] The nearest printed option is \(3.10\text{ cm}\), so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.93: The ball reverses direction with unchanged speed, so the magnitude of the momentum change is \[|\Delta p|=2mv=2(0.15)(12)=3.6\ \text{kg m s}^{-1}.\] By the impulse-momentum theorem \(F\,\Delta t=|\Delta p|\), so \[\Delta t=\frac{3.6}{100}=0.036\text{ s}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.94: Kinetic energy and momentum are related by \(K=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}\), so \(p=\sqrt{2mK}\). For equal kinetic energies, \[\frac{p_{1}}{p_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{1}}{m_{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{8}{2}}=2.\] The ratio is \(2:1\), so the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.95: Once joined by a wire the two spheres are at the same potential: \[\frac{kQ_{A}}{R_{A}}=\frac{kQ_{B}}{R_{B}}\;\Rightarrow\;\frac{Q_{A}}{Q_{B}}=\frac{R_{A}}{R_{B}}.\] The surface field is \(E=\frac{kQ}{R^{2}}\), so \[\frac{E_{A}}{E_{B}}=\frac{Q_{A}}{Q_{B}}\cdot\frac{R_{B}^{2}}{R_{A}^{2}}=\frac{R_{B}}{R_{A}}=\frac{10}{5}=2.\] The ratio is \(2:1\), so the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.96: Writing the wave as \(B_{y}=B_{0}\sin(kx-\omega t)\), the given form has \(k=5000\pi\ \text{m}^{-1}\) and \(\omega=4\times10^{11}\pi\ \text{s}^{-1}\), so the wave speed in the medium is \[v=\frac{\omega}{k}=\frac{4\times10^{11}\pi}{5000\pi}=8\times10^{7}\ \text{ms}^{-1}.\] Then \[E_{0}=vB_{0}=(8\times10^{7})(5\times10^{-6})=4\times10^{2}\ \text{Vm}^{-1}.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.97: Since \(n=c/v\), the medium with the smaller speed is the denser one. At the critical angle \(n_{d}\sin i_{c}=n_{r}\), so \[\sin i_{c}=\frac{n_{r}}{n_{d}}=\frac{v_{d}}{v_{r}}=\frac{1.5\times10^{8}}{2.0\times10^{8}}=\frac{3}{4}.\] Then \(\cos i_{c}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}\) and \(\tan i_{c}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{7}}\), so \(i_{c}=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{7}}\right)\). The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.98: With \(v=\frac{v_{e}}{3}\) and \(v_{e}^{2}=\frac{2GM}{R}\), energy conservation gives \[-\frac{GMm}{R}+\frac{1}{2}m\frac{v_{e}^{2}}{9}=-\frac{GMm}{R+h}.\] Substituting \(v_{e}^{2}=\frac{2GM}{R}\), \[\frac{GM}{R+h}=\frac{GM}{R}-\frac{GM}{9R}=\frac{8GM}{9R}\;\Rightarrow\;R+h=\frac{9R}{8}.\] Hence \(h=\frac{R}{8}=\frac{6400}{8}=800\text{ km}\), and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.99: The modulation index is \[\mu=\frac{V_{\max}-V_{\min}}{V_{\max}+V_{\min}}=\frac{60-20}{60+20}=\frac{40}{80}=0.5,\] i.e. \(50\%\). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.100: The parent nucleus is at rest, so by momentum conservation the two fragments carry equal and opposite momenta, \(|p_{1}|=|p_{2}|\). Since \(\lambda=\frac{h}{p}\), the two de Broglie wavelengths are equal irrespective of the mass split. The ratio is \(1:1\), so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.101: Total surface area of the box is \[A=2(0.6\times0.5+0.5\times0.2+0.2\times0.6)=2(0.30+0.10+0.12)=1.04\ \text{m}^{2}.\] The conduction rate through the \(1\text{ cm}\) wall is \[\frac{dQ}{dt}=\frac{KA\,\Delta T}{\ell}=\frac{(0.05)(1.04)(40)}{0.01}=208\ \text{W}.\] The melting rate is \[\frac{dm}{dt}=\frac{208}{3.4\times10^{5}}=6.1\times10^{-4}=61\times10^{-5}\ \text{kg s}^{-1}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.102: For a gas with \(n\) degrees of freedom, \(C_{V}=\frac{nR}{2}\) and \(C_{P}=C_{V}+R=\frac{(n+2)R}{2}\). Hence \[\frac{C_{V}}{C_{P}}=\frac{n}{n+2},\] so the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.103: For \(y=A\sin(\omega t-kx)\) with \(A=2\text{ cm}\), the maximum particle speed is \(A\omega\) and the wave speed is \(\frac{\omega}{k}\). Setting them equal, \[\frac{\omega}{k}=A\omega\;\Rightarrow\;k=\frac{1}{A}\;\Rightarrow\;\frac{2\pi}{\lambda}=\frac{1}{A}.\] Hence \(\lambda=2\pi A=4\pi\text{ cm}\), so the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.104: The two \(3\ \Omega\) resistors and the two \(6\ \Omega\) resistors form a Wheatstone bridge with the \(5\ \Omega\) resistor as the bridge arm.
